title: Module quiz: Claude's family and its surfaces

questions.stem: A team's research job runs for hours with nobody watching: mostly routine page fetching and note-taking, with a few hard judgment calls. Which design fits?

options.text: Hand it to managed agents with cheap workers and one strong decider
options.says: A job that runs for hours belongs in managed agents, and an orchestrator that hands bulk work to cheaper workers puts most tokens on the cheaper model while a stronger one takes the hard calls.

options.text: Chat through an app Project, with a person starting each step by hand
options.says: Ruled out because the apps give "Chat, Projects, artifacts, research, connectors; a person in the loop", and nobody is watching here.

options.text: Run the strongest tier through the Messages API on the team's own servers
options.says: Ruled out because the situation table points "A job runs for hours and should not tie up your servers" to managed agents.

options.text: Use the fastest tier for each step, then escalate only when the job fails
options.says: Ruled out because "the cheapest model for everything under-serves exactly the cases that need depth".

questions.stem: A feature must call one specific Claude model for two years. In review, someone flags the id hard-coded in the source. What is the most likely concern?

options.text: That snapshot has a retirement date, and nothing plans the move
options.says: The table shows retirement dates, and an id with a retirement date needs a migration plan before the date (the third trap).

options.text: Dated ids are rejected by the Messages API in favour of aliases
options.says: Ruled out because "For Haiku 4.5 the dated id is the snapshot and the shorter name is an alias", so dated ids are accepted.

options.text: A shorter alias would always follow new releases and should replace it
options.says: Ruled out because the page counts "including the dateless IDs used from the 4.6 generation on" among the pinned snapshots, so an alias is no more of a tracker.

options.text: Hard-coded ids bypass the pinned snapshot, so replies drift between calls
options.says: Ruled out because "every Claude model id is a pinned snapshot", so replies do not drift under a fixed id.

questions.stem: A team's helper remembered the conversation when it ran in an app chat. Rebuilt on the Messages API, it answers every message as if it were the first. What is the fix?

options.text: Turn on the endpoint's stored-chat setting for the account
options.says: Ruled out because "The API keeps nothing", so no account setting stores the chat.

options.text: Add "remember our history" to the system prompt
options.says: Ruled out because "The API sends only what you put in the request", and a sentence in the system prompt carries no history.

options.text: Include the prior exchange in the body of each call
options.says: Ownership of state decides where history lives: "The API keeps nothing; your code resends history", so each request must carry the earlier turns (the carry-across section).

options.text: Move the helper to a cloud platform that keeps the thread
options.says: Ruled out because the platforms offer "Same model family; different ids, access and sometimes features", and "a cloud platform adds its own identity and permission model", not a stored thread.

origin.section: One model, many surfaces: what carries across

questions.stem: A team calls the same Claude model through the Claude API and through Amazon Bedrock, reusing one config file with a single name string for both. Both platforms list the model as current and access is granted, but Bedrock answers that the name is unknown. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Bedrock runs a different generation of the family, so the name never matched
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "Same model family; different ids, access and sometimes features", so the generation is the same and only the id differs.

options.text: Each vendor gives the family its own id, so the value must differ
options.says: The cloud platforms bullet lists a separate id for each platform, for example anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Amazon Bedrock.

options.text: The account lacks the identity and permission setup that Bedrock requires
options.says: Ruled out because the scenario grants access and the error concerns the name: "The ids differ, and the platform sets its own dates".

options.text: Bedrock already retired that model, so its name is unknown there
options.says: Ruled out because the scenario says both platforms list the model as current, as the page's example "anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Amazon Bedrock" shows for a current model.
